### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**16** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5a47c49ef795781562a3ff3b012f5b573aa56354` — the merge of head `1a3854d288f1e5e2bac081863ee5281783bfe012` into base `bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5a47c49ef795781562a3ff3b012f5b573aa56354 && git checkout 5a47c49ef795781562a3ff3b012f5b573aa56354
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61 1a3854d288f1e5e2bac081863ee5281783bfe012 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61 && git merge --no-ff 1a3854d288f1e5e2bac081863ee5281783bfe012

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfca0efb79ac5df2049f392cdecd3bbeeea9ec61
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/business-unit-holders-complete.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/member-tier-holders-complete.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/team-position-holders-complete.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-queue-member.object.ts, packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts, docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md (D2, D6, D7 as amended)

Rendered 2026-11-05T05:37Z. Inputs: card #29604 (body and all eleven comments, the rulings 6594432222, 6599731698, 6600766777 and the seat's route-A ruling 6648946388 included), PR #30288 (body, eight-path file list, net diff against `main` at the head's merge base `771b2db2`), and the check-runs on the head. The narrowing face: no schema and no governed path in the diff; the floor is every path outside the prose faces, listed first above, then the files the hunks cite, read at the head (`refs/pm-review/30288-head`, fetched into a ref of my own; nothing checked out, built or run). CI on the head at posting time: every gate-carrying context (`Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–8, `Lint · *`, `Type Check · *`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`) concluded `success`; the UI and opt-in contexts `skipped`; no failure.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing at `openNodeRequest`** — a `team` or `position` approver (static, or an `expression` approver with `resolveAs` `team` / `position`) whose directory read throws now rejects with `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` from `resolveApproverSpec`'s directory catch (head :2757) and from `resolveExpressionApprovers`' catch (:3035), ahead of `slateNamesAPerson` and every `onEmptyApprovers` arm. The fallback slate (:4368) and the administrators slate (:4448) go through the same `expandApprovers` with the default `'refuse'`. Nothing is written before the primary expansion (:4309): the reads before it are the existing-request lookup, the live record and the submitter's acting addresses. **Right** — ADR-0142 D6 as amended; ruling 6599731698, letter B.
2. **The `queue` arm** — the throw sits in the catch, so it runs before the "expanded to nobody" return (:2803), which now also distinguishes a failed read from an empty queue on the literal reader. **Right as the ADR's execution point.** On this head it fires only when `expandMembers` itself rejects, and `OwnershipQueueService` on the same head never rejects: `expandSpec` (:322) catches to `[]` and `authoredMemberSpecs` (:516) to an empty map. So in the shipped composition a `sys_queue` / `sys_queue_member` / member-table outage behind a `queue` approver still opens the node on its policy. That is part 2's gap (route A, #30251), not made worse here — see ② and ④.
3. **`decideNode`'s pre-snapshot re-resolution** passes `'literal'` (:5113). **Right**: D6 puts the refusal at the node's open; a decision whose action row is already written must not be failed by a read made for its tally, and `main`'s answer there is kept unchanged.
4. **The cross-organization read filter** (`bounded`, :2715–2731) now rethrows a filter failure named as that read, inside the static resolver's try, so it refuses under the class naming the right read. **Right** (carried item 6600766777). In the expression resolver the same filter runs outside the try (:3047) — ④ should-fix 2.
5. **Types the ruling does not name** — `department` / `business_unit` / `bu`, `org_membership_level`, `manager`, `resolveAs: 'department'` — keep the literal slot and the #29362 warning. **Right**: 6599731698 names `queue`, `team`, `position` only, and `canonicalApproverType` folds only the deprecated `role` spelling, so the refusing set is closed.
6. **Public surface** — `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` is exported from the module and absent from `src/index.ts` (a named export list, no star export); `package.json` exposes only `.`. `expandApprovers` / `resolveApproverSpec` are private, their `onDirectoryFailure` parameter internal; `QUEUE_READ_LIMIT` was module-private. `packages/spec` is untouched and `IOwnershipQueueService` unchanged. **Right**: nothing published widens.
7. **plugin-sharing paging** — `queuesNaming`, `authoredQueueNames` and `authoredMemberSpecs` read through `readMembershipToCompletion` (keyset on `id`, pages of 10,000, `$and`-composed cursor, a refusal on a failed page or a walk it cannot vouch for). A widening at the consumer: a queue's 10,001st member is now a member. **Right** — the contract on `main` declares "the queue's members" with no bound, so the cap was an undeclared narrowing and this delivers the declared capability (reading 6591670782). A failed or unverifiable walk answers `[]` / `false` with one warn carrying the driver's reason — today's posture, which the route-A ruling says part 1 keeps. `authoredQueueRow` (one row by name) and `switchedOff` (bounded by `names.length`) are rightly left alone. `hasAnyQueue` now reads an organization's authored queue rows to the end to answer a boolean where it read at most 10,000; same work class, no contract change.
8. **The error carries no `code`**; it travels as class plus the `APPROVER_DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE:` prefix, the `NO_APPROVERS:` precedent in the same service — consistent. `retryable: true` is informational: `approval-node.ts` (:245) turns any throw into `{ success: false, error }` and nothing in the tree reads the property; the ruling's "retryable" is met by nothing having been written, so re-running the flow is the retry.
9. **Tests** — the new pins are top-level `describe`s in the components' shared harness files (ruling 6583487846); the three driver-sql pins move from "keeps the literal" to the refusal and keep the literal reader's old answer beside it; the queue double gained `$gt` and `orderBy`, and the page-2 failure case is faithful to `keysetWalk` (the first page carries the bare `where`, the second the `$and` cursor).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29604-approver-directory-refusal-queue-paging.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`; `!` in the title; a BREAKING banner; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset; one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, a category the gate names. No spec key, export or config field moves, so the Post-Task Checklist's rule applies: a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition. **Matches what the diff publishes.** The `(narrowing)` arm reads the narrowing face whichever word precedes it (`reviewFace`), which is the face this record serves. The changeset's `queue` sentence is read against the tree in ④ should-fix 1.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — right for the diff: the approval node's accept set narrows at open, and nothing on a published entry widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6648911579, open question 1 (the route): answered by the seat in 6648946388, route A; this PR is part 1 under it. Closed.
- Dev report 6650309375: `open_questions: []`. The decisions it states in the PR's acceptance notes, each read: (a) part 2 owes the service's own refusal, D7 and the D6 queue arm — consistent with the ruling; (b) unnamed types keep their answer — consistent with 6599731698; (c) the activation-ledger read keeps "switched on" when it fails — carried item 6600766777 asked that this be decided and said; it is said in the PR and the service header, and on D6/D7 it errs toward keeping people, never dropping them: accepted; (d) no `code` field — accepted on the `NO_APPROVERS:` precedent; (e) assignee and reviewers unset — the seat's hand-over step.
- Out-of-scope finding (dogfood permission-set clone door, `422` cloning `member_default`): carrier seat, noted; the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is `success`, so CI did not reproduce it. Not this PR's.
- `Skills-docs: none` — no page under `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` states the node's failed-read behaviour; the Docs Drift Check listed nothing. Accepted.
- Nothing outstanding; nothing escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against ADR-0142 D2 / D6 / D7 as amended on `main` and the cited code. The node refusal makes the spec's own refusal real: D6 as amended says the node refuses to open under every policy, with a class of its own naming the read, before `slateNamesAPerson` hands the slate to `onEmptyApprovers`, and the tree does exactly that, the `queue` early return consulting `directoryFailure` first. No declared capability is taken from a consumer: `onEmptyApprovers`'s declared input is the EMPTY slate (D2's "an empty expansion is a fact"); a failed read was never a declared input to it. The paging change delivers a capability the contract declared and the implementation had cut. Tried to break it: every `expandApprovers` caller takes `'refuse'` except the recorded-decision tally; no write precedes the primary expansion; the fallback and administrator slates are expanded by the same resolver; `resolveAs` admits only `user` / `department` / `position` / `team`, so the refusing set is closed; the literal reader answers as `main` did. The meantime after part 1 alone: a queue whose member tables fail still expands to nobody inside plugin-sharing, so D7 still revokes on it and the D6 queue arm still opens on the policy (the measured table in 6648911579). Both are ruled to part 2; nothing in this diff moves a failed-read answer, so part 1 leaves no new inconsistency and nothing less safe than `main`.

Findings:

- **should-fix 1 — the changeset's `queue` sentence (Prime Directive 10: a claim no wider than the enforcement).** The changeset — the text that ships as `CHANGELOG.md` — says a failed directory read behind a `queue` approver refuses the node, and its Clause-② line says the same. On this head that holds only when the ownership-queue service's `expandMembers` rejects, which the shipped service never does until part 2; a `sys_queue_member` or member-table outage behind a `queue` approver still opens on the policy. Narrow the `queue` wording in the changeset body and the Clause-② line to what ships ("a `queue` approver whose expansion rejects"), with one line saying the service's own member-table failures keep answering nobody until part 2. The PR body's acceptance note says this already; the changeset must too.
- **should-fix 2 — the expression resolver's filter sits outside the refusing try.** `resolveExpressionApprovers` calls `filterApproversWhoCanRead` after its catch (:3047), so a cross-organization filter failure on a `resolveAs: 'team' | 'position'` slate propagates as a raw error: the node still fails (`approval-node.ts` :245) but not under `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` and not naming the read, unlike the static path's `bounded`. Move the filter inside the try, or wrap it as `bounded` does, so both paths refuse under the one class. Narrow window: the filter keeps the slate on its own `sys_member` read failure.
- **should-fix 3 — a log line that states the wrong consequence.** `readFailureReason` logs a truncated walk's own sentence, which ends "so the expansion refuses instead" (`team-graph.ts` `holderReadRefusal`, expansion kind), while the queue service then answers nobody. Log the walk's reason without the consequence clause, or word the queue warning to say the answer it gave.

No must-fix.
